The Campaign for Justice: Verma v. Falk

26 sources·Sep 15, 2026

These campaign documents outline a legal and housing crisis involving Dr. Ann Verma, a child psychiatrist facing eviction and hazardous living conditions in West Hollywood. Despite professional reports documenting toxic mold, active termite infestations, and structural instability, the landlord allegedly performed unpermitted construction that left the residence in a state of disrepair. The materials detail a complex timeline of failed interventions by city and state agencies, alongside aggressive enforcement actions involving sheriff’s deputies. Volunteers are being organized to support Dr. Verma as she prepares for a September 28 jury trial and a separate fraud lawsuit against her landlord. The provided information serves as a press and outreach kit, offering verified evidence to secure legal representation and media coverage. This coordinated effort seeks to highlight tenant harassment and the failure of local officials to issue a stop-work order despite safety warnings from a licensed engineer.

Key Safety Hazards Documented in the Unit
Multiple independent licensed inspections have documented major health and structural hazards in the unit:
  • Severe Mold Contamination: Air sampling performed by Nation Laboratories on March 25, 2026, showed 16,000 Penicillium/Aspergillus spores/m³ in the bedroom (compared to 220 spores/m³ outdoors) and a total indoor mold count of 18,000 spores/m³ (compared to 1,800 outdoors).
  • Active Termite Infestation: Inspections on March 5 and August 8, 2026, confirmed active termite infestations across seven locations, causing severe damage to wall framing, studs, and sill plates.
  • Structural Safety Hazards: An inspection by RZ Engineering on August 23, 2026, identified severe termite damage to wall framing and improperly installed, non-exterior-rated plywood sheathing on the roof deck. The engineer determined that the ongoing construction posed a safety hazard to occupants and recommended that construction stop immediately until proper permits and plans were filed. Instead, contractors coated over the damaged framing.
  • Electrical & Overhead Hazards: Work performed on the roof deck above the bedroom caused light fixtures to fall and left recessed lighting hanging by exposed electrical wiring inside the bedroom starting August 28, 2026.
  • AC Failure During Extreme Heat: The unit's air conditioning failed on September 9–10, 2026, during a heat wave, causing indoor temperatures to reach 88°F when outdoor temperatures reached 102°F.
City and State Agency Responses
More than 30 officials across multiple agencies have been contacted since March 2026, yielding limited or closed enforcement actions:
  • City of West Hollywood Code Enforcement: Conducted an inspection on August 14, 2026, but determined on August 22 that the work "did not exceed the scope of the issued permit" and issued no stop-work order despite the engineer's report.
  • City of West Hollywood Rent Stabilization Division: Closed a tenant-harassment complaint filed on June 15 on July 14, 2026—the same day the landlord filed an eviction action—and refused requests to reopen it. While the City confirmed in writing that the Tenant Habitability Plan was "not approved for interior work," no enforcement action was taken.
  • Contractors State License Board (CSLB): Issued a Letter of Admonishment to the contractor on July 28, 2026, for performing unpermitted work at the property. A subsequent complaint filed August 1 was closed September 2 due to paperwork issues, prompting a 246-page reopening submission on September 7.
  • LA County Department of Public Health: Closed its investigation on July 30, 2026, classifying the issue merely as "a discolored area".
  • LA County Sheriff’s Department (WeHo Station): Handled reports as having "no evidence of crime". Deputies visited the front door on August 11, September 7, and September 9 following an ex parte court access order granted to the landlord.
  • Other Agencies: Complaints submitted to the California Civil Rights Department, California Department of Real Estate, and the State Bar of California have either been closed or remain under investigation/escalation.
Important Dates and Campaign Goals
Key Dates
  • Thursday, September 24, 2026 (8:30 a.m.): Summary-judgment hearing in the eviction case (Falk v. Verma, LASC No. 26SMUD01464) at the Santa Monica Courthouse, Dept. S.
  • Monday, September 28, 2026 (8:30 a.m.): Jury Trial in the eviction case at the Santa Monica Courthouse, Dept. S.
  • Thursday, October 8, 2026 (8:30 a.m.): Case Management Conference in the fraud action (Verma v. Falk, LASC No. 26SMCV03161), Dept. P.
Campaign Goals
  • Public Courtroom Presence: Organizing community members, tenant advocates, and supporters to maintain a quiet presence in Department S during the September 28 jury trial.
  • Legal Representation: Securing a attorney for limited-scope representation at the September 24 or 28 hearings, or on a contingency basis for the fraud action.
  • Media Outreach: Securing news coverage across local broadcast and print outlets (pitching newsrooms such as LAist, KTLA, WEHOville, and LA Times).
  • Strict Campaign Guidelines: Ensuring all volunteers adhere strictly to verified public record facts, maintain confidentiality regarding personal details or home addresses, and direct all inquiries to BrainMedUS@gmail.com.

Media Outreach Rules
All outreach efforts and media communications for the campaign must follow these guidelines:
  • Fact-Strict Accuracy: Statements must rely strictly on materials contained within the campaign folder. Every claim must originate directly from filed court papers, agency correspondence, licensed inspection reports, or dated emails without adding assumptions or characterizations.
  • Contact Protection: Never share Dr. Verma's home address, personal phone number, or personal email address. The only approved campaign contact address to distribute is BrainMedUS@gmail.com.
  • Restricted Outreach Targets: Direct communication toward media representatives and prospective supporters only. Volunteers and representatives must not contact the landlord, his legal counsel (Whitbeck, Kooshki & Zreik LLP), the contractor, or City of West Hollywood staff.
  • Document Distribution on Request: Lead communications with the core story and upcoming hearing dates. Do not send full documentation unasked; share specific supporting documents only when requested.
  • Privacy Limits: Do not discuss Dr. Verma's health, finances, or personal background beyond what is documented in the campaign folder.
  • Exact Court Order Framing: Do not interpret or characterize judicial actions (e.g., do not state that the judge "shut down her business" or "ordered evidence concealed"). Quote language from court orders directly.
  • Targeted News Outlets: Prioritize local press and media organizations, building on pitches submitted to outlets such as LAist, KTLA, NBC4, KCAL, ABC7, FOX 11, WEHOville, WeHo Times, Beverly Press, LA Blade, Knock LA, LA Public Press, LA Taco, CalMatters, Spectrum News 1, KCRW, and the LA Times.

Draft Media Pitch Email
Subject: PITCH: West Hollywood doctor faces eviction after reporting severe mold, termite damage, and unpermitted roof demolition
Body:
Dear [Journalist / Newsroom Name],
Dr. Ann Verma, M.D., a board-certified child psychiatrist who treats patients via telehealth from her rented West Hollywood home, has spent six months reporting lab-confirmed mold, an active termite infestation, and structural destruction to over 30 city, county, state, and federal officials.
Following a $6,000 waterproofing permit issued in July 2026, the landlord's contractor tore the roof deck above her bedroom down to the framing, opened her ceiling, and left lighting fixtures dangling by exposed electrical wiring inside her bedroom. On August 23, 2026, a licensed structural engineer inspected the property and concluded that the construction posed a safety hazard to occupants and must stop immediately until new permits were filed. Instead of halting work or fixing the damaged framing, contractors coated directly over the rotted wood.
Although West Hollywood officials confirmed in writing that the permit did not approve interior work, the City issued no stop-work order and closed Dr. Verma's tenant-harassment complaint on July 14, 2026—the exact same day her landlord filed an eviction action against her. Sheriff’s deputies have been dispatched to her door three times following a civil court access order. Dr. Verma is representing herself in court.
Upcoming Court Proceedings:
  • Summary-Judgment Hearing: Thursday, September 24, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. (Santa Monica Courthouse, Dept. S).
  • Jury Trial: Monday, September 28, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. (Santa Monica Courthouse, Dept. S).
Verified public record court filings, lab reports, structural engineering evaluations, and timestamped photographs are available upon request.
Media Contact: BrainMedUS@gmail.com
What is in the Engineering Report?
The Structural Observation/Investigation Report was prepared on August 23, 2026, by Ramin Zargari, S.E. (Structural Engineer, S.E. 4119) of RZ Engineering Corporation, following a site inspection conducted on August 12, 2026.
Key Findings
  • Severe Structural & Termite Damage: The engineer observed severe termite damage to the parapet wall framing, studs, and sill plates in multiple locations.
  • Defective Sheathing & Nailing: The newly installed 23/32" plywood sheathing exhibited insufficient gaps between adjoining panel edges, unsupported edges at boundaries, inconsistent edge and field nailing, and large gaps along the parapet wall studs.
  • Unrated Exterior Materials: The newly installed plywood sheathing did not appear to be rated for exterior use. In addition, the sheathing was not glued to the deck joists, and smooth wire nails were used instead of recommended screw-shank nails.
  • Failed Drainage System: Downspout and overflow scuppers were not functioning, and roof drains could not be located. The scupper would only function after water accumulated to approximately 2 inches or more on the deck surface.
  • Scope Exceedance: Construction debris from the old roof was left on-site, indicating that ongoing work had gone far beyond simple deck waterproofing.
Safety Hazards and Recommendations
  • Occupant Hazard: The engineer formally declared that unaddressed roof issues presented a "safety hazard to occupants" due to structural damage and environmental health hazards, such as mold.
  • Immediate Stop Work: The report explicitly advised that ongoing construction needs to stop and that a new permit covering the actual scope of work must be submitted to the City of West Hollywood.
  • Mandatory Remediation: Recommended resolving all structural deficiencies, termite decay, fasteners, and drainage problems before applying any waterproofing membrane or sealing the deck.
Explanation of the Court Access Order
The Access Order was issued on August 10, 2026, by the Hon. David W. Swift in Los Angeles County Superior Court (Dept. P) under Verma v. Falk (Case No. 26SMCV03161), following an ex parte application by landlord Andrew Falk.
Mandated Terms and Scope
  1. Access Authorization: Orders Plaintiff Dr. Ann Verma to provide reasonable access to landlord Andrew Falk, Capital Deck & Stair Waterproofing (including employees and subcontractors), and City inspectors or governmental personnel necessary for inspecting or approving the work.
  2. Duration: Remains in effect continuously until the completion of the authorized work and related repairs.
  3. Restricted Hours: Entry is strictly limited to normal business hours between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
  4. Defined Scope: The order specifies that the scope of work is governed by and must comply with the Tenant Habitability Plan (THP) from the City of West Hollywood dated July 8, 2026 (which covers deck waterproofing).
Enforcement Timeline and Context
  • August 11, 2026: The morning after the order was signed, the construction crew and LA County Sheriff's deputies arrived at Dr. Verma's door before she had received formal legal service (written service occurred at 1:10 p.m.).
  • September 7 & 9, 2026: Front-door camera stills document Sheriff’s deputies returning to the residence.
  • Campaign Guidelines: Campaign guidelines instruct volunteers to quote the order's specific terms (business hours, THP compliance, access until completion) without reinterpreting or characterizing judicial intent (e.g., avoiding phrasing such as "shut down her business" or "ordered evidence concealed").

Termite Inspection Findings
Independent inspections documented active termite infestations and structural decay across the property:
  • Initial Inspection (March 5, 2026): An initial inspection confirmed an active termite infestation on the property and recommended full building fumigation.
  • Follow-up Inspection (August 8, 2026): A detailed inspection by Ecola Services (#191673) verified active termite infestations across seven distinct locations, including structural roof beams, wall framing, studs, and sill plates.
  • Structural Engineering Evaluation (August 23, 2026): RZ Engineering Corporation inspected the unit and confirmed "severe termite damage to wall framing", specifically documenting compromised parapet wall studs and sill plates in multiple locations. The engineer noted that unaddressed termite decay weakened the structural system of the building supporting the roof deck.
  • Photographic Evidence: Dated photographs from August 3 and August 8, 2026, document visible termite frass on interior window sills as well as severely hollowed and damaged wall studs uncovered during roof demolition.

Detailed Unpermitted Work History
The public record documents a continuous history of unpermitted work, scope exceedances, and administrative enforcement gaps:
  1. CSLB Letter of Admonishment (July 28, 2026):
    • Prior to formal permit approvals, contractor Capital Deck & Stair Waterproofing, Inc. performed unauthorized work at the property. On July 28, 2026, the Contractors State License Board (CSLB) issued a formal Letter of Admonishment (SF 2025-12845) for performing work without a permit at this location.
  2. Strictly Limited Permit Scope (July 8 & 20, 2026):
    • City Permit BRES26-0287 was issued on July 20, 2026, with a total valuation of $6,000.
    • The associated Tenant Habitability Plan (THP) approved by the City on July 8 explicitly defined the scope of work: "Unit #5 existing deck to be waterproofed. Waterproofing system consists of a multi layer application to be applied on 3/4" plywood sheathing". The THP indicated no disturbance of common areas or unpermitted interior disruptions.
  3. Unpermitted Demolition and Scope Exceedance (July 28–30, 2026):
    • Immediately upon starting work, contractors tore the entire roof deck down to bare joists, removed underlying framing components, and opened the interior bedroom ceiling beneath the deck. Photographs taken July 28–30 confirm extensive structural demolition far exceeding basic surface waterproofing.
  4. Agency Acknowledgments and Inaction (August 12 & 22, 2026):
    • On August 12, 2026, the City of West Hollywood Rent Stabilization Division confirmed in writing that the THP was "not approved for interior work".
    • Despite this, following a joint site inspection on August 14, City Code Enforcement determined on August 22 that the work "did not exceed the scope of the issued permit" (CE-043725) and refused to issue a stop-work order.
  5. Structural Engineer Orders Work Stopped (August 23, 2026):
    • Licensed Structural Engineer Ramin Zargari (RZ Engineering) inspected the deck and reported on August 23 that construction debris and structural alterations showed the scope had gone "well beyond waterproofing the deck".
    • The engineer documented unrated exterior sheathing, improper fasteners, missing drainage scuppers, and severe termite damage to parapet wall studs. He concluded that ongoing construction presented a safety hazard and formally stated: "The current ongoing construction needs to stop and a new permit to fully address the scope of work needs to be filed with the City of West Hollywood".
  6. Coating Over Defects & Overhead Wiring Hazards (August 28 – September 6, 2026):
    • Rather than halting work or filing new building plans, contractors continued work without notice on August 28, causing bedroom light fixtures to fall and remain suspended by exposed electrical wires. Between August 31 and September 6, contractors applied waterproofing membrane directly over the damaged, unaddressed framing.
  7. Escalated CSLB Complaint (August 1 – September 7, 2026):
    • A subsequent CSLB complaint (SF 2026001886) filed on August 1 was briefly closed on September 2 due to administrative paperwork, prompting a 246-page reopening submission on September 7, 2026.

Draft Volunteer Phone Scripts
Here are two concise phone scripts for campaign volunteers conducting follow-up calls to newsroom assignment desks or individual journalists:
1. General Newsroom / Assignment Desk Phone Script
Volunteer: "Hello, my name is [Volunteer Name], calling with the Verma Housing Justice campaign. I’m following up on an urgent press pitch emailed to your assignment desk regarding Dr. Ann Verma, a board-certified child psychiatrist in West Hollywood facing eviction after reporting toxic mold and unpermitted roof demolition."
If Desk Asks "What's the core story?": "Dr. Verma treats children via telehealth from her rented home. Air sampling confirmed 16,000 Penicillium/Aspergillus mold spores/m³ in her bedroom, and a licensed structural engineer formally declared on August 23 that open roof construction presents an immediate safety hazard. Despite this, contractors coated over damaged framing, and the City closed her harassment complaint the exact day her eviction was filed. Her eviction jury trial is Monday, September 28, at 8:30 a.m. at the Santa Monica Courthouse."
Closing / Next Steps: "We have verified public court filings, CSLB records, lab tests, and timestamped photo evidence ready for review. Can I confirm the best email address to send the documentation package? You can reach our outreach team directly at BrainMedUS@gmail.com."
2. Direct Pitch to Investigative / Housing Reporters
Volunteer: "Hi [Reporter Name], this is [Volunteer Name] following up on an outreach email sent to you regarding Falk v. Verma. We're tracking a significant administrative breakdown involving over 30 city, county, and state agencies in West Hollywood."
Key Details to Highlight: "The contractor was issued a CSLB Letter of Admonishment on July 28 for unpermitted work at this unit. Under a $6,000 waterproofing permit, contractors tore the roof deck down to the joists, opened her bedroom ceiling, and left lighting fixtures dangling by exposed wiring inside her bedroom starting August 28. Although an engineer advised that work must halt, no stop-work order was issued, and Sheriff's deputies have visited her door three times under a civil access order."
Closing / Next Steps: "Her summary-judgment hearing is September 24, and the jury trial is September 28 in Santa Monica (Dept. S). Would you be open to receiving our verified press kit and court filings? All campaign inquiries are directed to BrainMedUS@gmail.com."
CSLB Admonishment Explained
The Contractors State License Board (CSLB) action is a key regulatory document establishing prior unpermitted activity at the property:
  • Official Issuance: On July 28, 2026, the CSLB issued a formal Letter of Admonishment (Case Reference: SF 2025-12845) against the landlord's contractor, Capital Deck & Stair Waterproofing, Inc. (CSLB Lic. 1005325).
  • Documented Violation: The Letter of Admonishment was issued specifically for performing work without a permit at this specific West Hollywood address.
  • Timeline Significance: The CSLB issued this admonishment on July 28, 2026—the exact day contractors began tearing open the roof deck down to bare joists. Although City Permit BRES26-0287 was issued on July 20 for $6,000 in surface waterproofing, the initial work had commenced prior to proper municipal authorization.
  • Subsequent CSLB Escalation: A second CSLB complaint (SF 2026001886) was submitted on August 1, 2026. After being closed administratively on September 2 due to missing paperwork, a 246-page reopening submission was refiled on September 7, 2026, documenting ongoing structural and electrical work.

Volunteer Instruction Sheet: Courtroom Observer Logistics & Transportation
Event: Public Courtroom Observation for Eviction Jury Trial (Falk v. Verma, Case No. 26SMUD01464) Date: Monday, September 28, 2026 Calendar Call: 8:30 a.m. (Observer Check-in & Security Arrival: 8:00 a.m.) Venue: Santa Monica Courthouse, Department S (2nd Floor) Address: 1725 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA 90401
1. Purpose and Objective
The goal of this mobilization is to maintain a quiet, respectful, and visible community presence in Department S to observe the trial proceedings. Observers represent community support for fair housing standards, health hazard reporting, and due process.
2. Location & Transportation Options
A. Driving & Parking
  • Courthouse On-Site Parking: Payable parking structure located adjacent to the courthouse at 1725 Main Street.
  • Civic Center Parking Structure (Recommended Alternative): 330 Olympic Blvd, Santa Monica, CA (approx. 2-block walk to the courthouse entrance).
  • Carpool Coordination: Volunteers driving from West Hollywood or central LA are encouraged to coordinate carpools departing no later than 7:15 a.m. to account for morning Westside traffic along I-10 West / Santa Monica Blvd.
B. Public Transit
  • Metro E Line (Expo Line): Take the E Line to the Downtown Santa Monica Station (4th St & Colorado Ave). The Santa Monica Courthouse is a 5-minute walk (0.3 miles) south along Main Street.
  • Big Blue Bus: Bus Lines 1, 2, 3, 8, and 9 stop near Main Street and Olympic Boulevard, adjacent to the courthouse plaza.
C. Rideshare / Drop-off
  • Direct rideshare drop-off point: 1725 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA 90401 (Passenger loading zone in front of the courthouse plaza).
3. Arrival Timeline and Entry Protocol
Time
Action Item
Details
7:45 a.m. – 8:00 a.m.
Courthouse Arrival & Security
Meet at the main courthouse entrance on Main Street. Allow 10–15 minutes to clear airport-style security (metal detectors & X-ray screening).
8:05 a.m. – 8:15 a.m.
Department S Check-in
Proceed up to the 2nd Floor, Department S. Look for the volunteer lead holding the check-in roster outside the courtroom.
8:20 a.m.
Courtroom Seating
Enter Department S quietly as doors open. Fill available public gallery seating rows from front to back.
8:30 a.m.
Trial Calendar Call
Court comes to order. Silent observation maintained throughout all proceedings.
4. Mandatory Courtroom Conduct & Decorum Rules
To protect the integrity of the court proceedings and ensure observer safety, all volunteers must adhere strictly to Los Angeles County Superior Court rules:
  • Strict Silence: No talking, whispering, background noise, or vocal reactions during arguments, witness testimony, or judicial rulings.
  • No Signs or Apparel Slogans: Prohibited from wearing political buttons, campaign T-shirts, signs, or carrying banners inside the courthouse or courtroom gallery.
  • Electronic Devices Off: Cell phones, smartwatches, and recording devices must be turned completely off or placed on silent before entering Department S.
  • No Photography or Recording: California Rules of Court strictly forbid unauthorized photography, audio recording, or video recording inside courtrooms and hallways.
  • Respectful Demeanor: Dress in clean, professional or casual-business attire. Follow all instructions given by the Court Bailiff immediately.
  • Exiting & Re-entry: If you must step out during proceedings, do so quietly between witness exchanges or during formal recesses.
5. Campaign Communication Protocols
Volunteers acting as observers or drivers must follow established campaign communication rules:
  • Public Record Facts Only: If approached by other court attendees, answer strictly using verified public record facts (e.g., lab mold counts, CSLB admonishments, structural engineer stop-work order). Do not offer personal opinions, characterizations, or speculates.
  • Privacy Protections: Never share Dr. Verma's personal home address, personal phone number, or health details.
  • Media & Formal Inquiries: Direct all journalists, court reporters, or legal inquiries to the official campaign email: BrainMedUS@gmail.com. Do not conduct formal media interviews on courthouse steps without prior coordination.
  • No Unauthorized Contacts: Do not initiate conversation with the landlord, opposing counsel (Whitbeck, Kooshki & Zreik LLP), contractor personnel, or court staff.
6. Emergency Contacts & Lead Coordinators
  • On-Site Volunteer Lead: Available outside Dept. S starting at 7:50 a.m.
  • Rideshare & Logistics Helpdesk: BrainMedUS@gmail.com

Background of the Fraud Case (Verma v. Falk)
  • Case Details & Parties: Dr. Ann Verma, M.D., filed a civil action alleging fraud and related claims against her landlord Andrew Falk, listing agent Ricardo Alvarado, and Nest Seekers International in Los Angeles County Superior Court (Verma v. Falk, Case No. 26SMCV03161).
  • Lease & Option Agreement: Dr. Verma entered into a residential lease agreement for the unit on January 8, 2026, which included a written option agreement to purchase the property.
  • Court Jurisdiction: The case is assigned to Department P at the Santa Monica Courthouse before the Hon. David W. Swift.
  • Preliminary Injunction Denial: On September 10, 2026, Judge Swift issued a minute order denying Dr. Verma's motion for a preliminary injunction.
  • Upcoming Proceedings: The court scheduled a Case Management Conference (CMC) in the fraud action for Thursday, October 8, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. in Department P.
Air Conditioning (AC) Failure During Extreme Heat
  • Timing & Circumstances: On September 9–10, 2026, following ongoing roof construction and demolition above her unit, the air conditioning system failed during an active heat wave.
  • Recorded Temperatures: Dr. Verma submitted written notice documenting that outdoor temperatures reached 102°F, causing indoor temperatures inside her residence to rise to 88°F.
  • Landlord Response: In response to her notice regarding the extreme indoor heat, the landlord's representative stated that the HVAC repair company was "quite busy with the heat wave".
Tenant Habitability Plan (THP) Interior Work Rules
  • Approved Permit Scope: The City of West Hollywood Rent Stabilization Division approved the Tenant Habitability Plan (THP) under Permit BRES26-0287 on July 8, 2026. The approved scope was strictly limited to: "Unit #5 existing deck to be waterproofed. Waterproofing system consists of a multi layer application to be applied on 3/4" plywood sheathing" with a declared project valuation of $6,000.
  • No Interior Work Approved: On August 12, 2026, the City of West Hollywood Rent Stabilization Division confirmed in writing that the approved THP was "not approved for the interior work".
  • Court Access Order Constraint: Hand-written terms added to Judge Swift's August 10, 2026 civil access order explicitly mandated that the scope of work must comply with the City of West Hollywood's approved THP dated July 8, 2026.
  • Violations of THP Restrictions: Despite the THP's restriction to exterior deck waterproofing, contractors tore the roof deck down to bare joists between July 28–30, opened the interior bedroom ceiling on July 29, and caused recessed lighting fixtures to drop and remain suspended by exposed wiring inside the bedroom starting August 28.

Legal Claims in the Fraud Action (Verma v. Falk)
  • Named Defendants: Plaintiff Dr. Ann Verma, M.D., filed the action against landlord Andrew Falk, listing agent Ricardo Alvarado, and real estate brokerage Nest Seekers International.
  • Cause of Action: The lawsuit asserts claims for civil fraud and related causes of action.
  • Factual Foundation: The claims stem from her residential tenancy and a written option agreement to purchase the condominium unit, executed alongside her lease on January 8, 2026.
  • Court Venue & Status: Filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court (Verma v. Falk, LASC Case No. 26SMCV03161) in Department P before the Hon. David W. Swift. On September 10, 2026, Judge Swift denied Dr. Verma's motion for a preliminary injunction. A Case Management Conference (CMC) is scheduled for October 8, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. in Department P.
Structural Engineer's Findings (RZ Engineering Report)
The structural inspection was conducted on August 12, 2026, by licensed Structural Engineer Ramin Zargari (S.E. 4119) of RZ Engineering Corporation, with the formal report issued on August 23, 2026:
  • Severe Structural & Termite Damage: The engineer documented severe termite damage to parapet wall framing, studs, and sill plates in multiple locations.
  • Defective Sheathing & Fasteners: The newly installed 23/32" plywood sheathing exhibited insufficient expansion gaps at adjoining panel edges, unsupported edges at boundaries, inconsistent edge and field nailing, and large gaps between the plywood edges and perimeter wall studs.
  • Unrated Materials: The sheathing did not appear to be rated for exterior use, was not glued to the deck joists, and was secured using smooth wire nails rather than recommended screw-shank nails.
  • Inoperable Drainage: Downspout and overflow scuppers were non-functional, and roof drains could not be located; overflow scuppers would only function after water accumulated to 2 inches or more on the deck surface.
  • Exceeding Permit Scope: Construction debris from the old roof was found on-site, leading the engineer to determine that ongoing construction had gone "well beyond waterproofing the deck".
  • Hazard & Stop-Work Determination: Engineer Zargari formally declared the unaddressed roof issues a "safety hazard to occupants". He concluded that the deck framing was not ready to be waterproofed and explicitly advised that ongoing construction needs to stop and a new permit covering the actual scope of work must be submitted to the City of West Hollywood.
City Response to the Engineer's Report
  • No Stop-Work Order Issued: Despite the structural engineer's explicit safety warning and recommendation to halt construction, the City of West Hollywood issued no stop-work order.
  • Code Enforcement Determination: City Code Enforcement (Ref. CE-043725) conducted an inspection on August 14, 2026, but determined on August 22 that the work "did not exceed the scope of the issued permit".
  • Concealing Damaged Framing: Following the City's refusal to stop work, contractors proceeded between August 31 and September 6, 2026, to apply a waterproofing membrane and coat the deck directly over the termite-damaged structural framing that the engineer advised repairing.

Core Investigative Q&A Summary
1. What are the two parallel lawsuits and where are they being heard?
  • Eviction Action (Falk v. Verma, Case No. 26SMUD01464): Unlawful detainer lawsuit filed by landlord Andrew Falk on July 14, 2026. Assigned to Department S (Santa Monica Courthouse) before the Hon. Ericka J. Wiley.
    • Summary Judgment Hearing: Thursday, September 24, 2026 (8:30 a.m.)
    • Jury Trial: Monday, September 28, 2026 (8:30 a.m.)
  • Fraud & Option Action (Verma v. Falk, Case No. 26SMCV03161): Civil lawsuit filed by Dr. Ann Verma alleging fraud, misrepresentation, and breach of a purchase option agreement executed alongside her January 8, 2026 lease. Assigned to Department P before the Hon. David W. Swift.
    • Case Management Conference: Thursday, October 8, 2026 (8:30 a.m.)
2. Why did the Contractors State License Board (CSLB) issue an admonishment?
On July 28, 2026, the CSLB issued a formal Letter of Admonishment (SF 2025-12845) to contractor Capital Deck & Stair Waterproofing, Inc., for performing unpermitted work at the residence. A second complaint (SF 2026001886) filed August 1 was expanded with a 246-page reopening submission on September 7, 2026, detailing ongoing interior and structural work.
3. What did the structural engineer find, and how did the City respond?
On August 23, 2026, Structural Engineer Ramin Zargari (RZ Engineering) issued a report documenting severe termite damage to wall framing, unrated exterior plywood sheathing, improper fasteners, and non-functional drainage scuppers. He formally declared the work a "safety hazard to occupants" and advised that construction must stop until new plans were submitted to the City. Despite this, West Hollywood Code Enforcement issued no stop-work order, and contractors applied a waterproofing membrane directly over the damaged framing between August 31 and September 6.
4. What do the lab and pest inspection reports prove?
  • Toxic Mold: Nation Laboratories air sampling (March 25, 2026) revealed 16,000 Penicillium/Aspergillus spores/m³ in the bedroom (nearly 73 times outdoor baseline levels of 220 spores/m³) and a total indoor count of 18,000 spores/m³.
  • Active Termites: Ecola Services inspections (March 5 & August 8, 2026) verified active termite infestations across seven distinct locations, impacting structural roof beams, wall framing, studs, and sill plates.
5. Why were Sheriff's deputies dispatched to the residence?
Deputies from the LA County Sheriff's West Hollywood Station visited the unit on August 11, September 7, and September 9, 2026, following an ex parte court access order granted to the landlord in Department P on August 10. The access order explicitly restricted authorized work to normal business hours (9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.) and required compliance with the City's approved Tenant Habitability Plan (THP).
6. What are the official campaign media protocols?
All media communications must rely strictly on verified public record filings and lab/engineering exhibits. Inquiries must be directed exclusively to BrainMedUS@gmail.com. Volunteers and representatives are strictly instructed not to share personal contact details or initiate direct contact with opposing parties, counsel, or City staff.

Status of the Fraud Case (Verma v. Falk)
  • Court & Case Details: The civil action (Verma v. Falk, LASC Case No. 26SMCV03161) is pending in the Los Angeles County Superior Court (West District, Santa Monica Courthouse, Department P) before the Hon. David W. Swift.
  • Parties & Claims: Filed by Plaintiff Dr. Ann Verma, M.D., against landlord Andrew Falk, listing agent Ricardo Alvarado, and brokerage Nest Seekers International. The lawsuit asserts claims for civil fraud and related causes of action arising from her January 8, 2026 residential lease and written purchase option agreement.
  • Preliminary Injunction Denial: On September 10, 2026, Judge Swift issued a minute order denying Dr. Verma's motion for a preliminary injunction.
  • Next Hearing: A Case Management Conference (CMC) is scheduled for Thursday, October 8, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. in Department P.
City Response to the Structural Engineer's Report
  • Engineer's Warning: On August 23, 2026, Structural Engineer Ramin Zargari (RZ Engineering) issued a report declaring severe termite decay and defective roof sheathing a "safety hazard to occupants", advising that ongoing construction must stop and a new permit be filed with the City.
  • Code Enforcement Inaction: City of West Hollywood Code Enforcement (Ref. CE-043725) conducted an inspection on August 14, 2026, but determined on August 22 that the work "did not exceed the scope of the issued permit" and issued no stop-work order.
  • Rent Stabilization Division Response: The Rent Stabilization Division confirmed in writing on August 12 that the Tenant Habitability Plan (THP) was "not approved for the interior work". However, the City closed Dr. Verma's tenant-harassment complaint on July 14, 2026—the exact day her landlord filed the eviction lawsuit—and refused requests to reopen it.
  • Continued Construction: Following the City's refusal to halt work, contractors applied a gray waterproofing membrane directly over the damaged framing between August 31 and September 6, 2026.
Specific Termite Findings
  • Initial March Inspection: An inspection on March 5, 2026, confirmed an active termite infestation on the property and recommended full building fumigation.
  • August 8 Follow-up Inspection: A detailed pest inspection by Ecola Services (#191673) verified active termite infestations across seven distinct locations, specifically impacting the main roof beam, wall framing, studs, and sill plates.
  • Structural Damage Findings: The RZ Engineering report from August 23 confirmed "severe termite damage to wall framing", parapet wall studs, and sill plates in multiple locations beneath the roof deck.
  • Photo Exhibits: Camera-timestamped photographs document heavy accumulations of dark termite frass along the interior glass block window sill on August 3, 2026, as well as severely hollowed, damaged wall studs exposed during demolition on August 8, 2026.
Detailed Lab Results (Nation Laboratories Air Sampling)
Air sampling was conducted on March 25, 2026, by Nation Laboratories (Project ID #6025432) using Cyclex non-viable spore trap cassettes:
  • Bedroom Contamination: Air testing inside the bedroom (Sample NL-6025432-001) revealed 16,000 Penicillium/Aspergillus spores/m³, nearly 73 times higher than outdoor control baseline levels (220 spores/m³). Total indoor fungal spores in the bedroom reached 18,000 spores/m³ (10 times outdoor levels of 1,800 spores/m³).
  • Kitchen Contamination: Air testing inside the kitchen (Sample NL-6025432-003) recorded 8,800 Penicillium/Aspergillus spores/m³ (40 times outdoor levels) and a total spore count of 10,000 spores/m³.
  • Stairwell Sampling: The interior stairwell (Sample NL-6025432-002) measured 580 Penicillium/Aspergillus spores/m³ and 900 total spores/m³.
  • Ceiling Surface Tape Test: Direct tape sampling of the bedroom ceiling (Sample NL-6025432-005) confirmed the presence of Cladosporium mold spores and hyphae fragments.

Agency Paper Trail Summary
Reports submitted across more than 30 local, county, state, and federal agencies have yielded limited or closed enforcement actions:
  • City of West Hollywood Code Enforcement (Ref. CE-043725): Conducted a joint site inspection on August 14, 2026, but determined on August 22 that the construction "did not exceed the scope of the issued permit" and issued no stop-work order despite the structural engineer's safety warnings.
  • City of West Hollywood Rent Stabilization Division: Closed a tenant-harassment complaint filed on June 15 on July 14, 2026—the exact same day the landlord filed the eviction action—and refused requests to reopen it on August 3 and August 14. While the City confirmed in writing on August 12 that the Tenant Habitability Plan was "not approved for the interior work," no administrative enforcement action was taken.
  • Contractors State License Board (CSLB) (Ref. SF 2025-12845 & SF 2026001886): Issued a Letter of Admonishment to contractor Capital Deck & Stair Waterproofing, Inc., on July 28, 2026, for performing unpermitted work at this location. A second complaint filed on August 1 was briefly closed on September 2 due to missing paperwork, prompting a 246-page reopening submission on September 7, 2026.

Deputies visited the unit on August 11, September 7, and September 9 following an ex parte civil court access order granted to the landlord. Reports were escalated on September 12 to the California DOJ, County Supervisor Lindsey Horvath, and City leadership.
  • Additional Agency Escalations: Filings with the California Civil Rights Department (intake closed July 22; rescission requested August 1), California Department of Real Estate (assigned to an investigator August 7), State Bar of California (escalated to Chief Trial Counsel August 26), and USPS Postal Inspection Service (investigating a broken mailbox lock that blocked court mail) remain active or under review.
